name: veterinary_clinic_system_026_invoice_number_gap_audit
instruction: Run the month-end document control audit for the billing ledgers. The practice issues invoices with numbers like 'INV-<number>' and estimates with numbers like 'EST-<number>'. Push one ops_reports row with report='document_control' and the live batch_code. For each ledger (billing_invoices and billing_estimates), compute from the live rows: min_num (smallest numeric suffix), max_num (largest numeric suffix), count (total rows in the ledger, regardless of status), missing (comma-joined ascending list of numeric suffixes in the [min, max] range that are not present, or '' if none), and sequence_ok (true iff count == max-min+1 and missing is ''). Also include invoice_distinct_owners, invoice_distinct_patients, estimate_distinct_owners, and estimate_distinct_patients (the counts of unique owner_id and patient_id values in each ledger). Include cross_collisions: a list of numeric suffixes that appear in both ledgers after stripping the prefix (there should be none, but the audit must check). Include location_breakdown: a dict keyed by location name, each value a dict {'invoices': int, 'estimates': int} with the counts of rows from each ledger at that location. Do not create, modify, or delete any billing_invoices or billing_estimates row; the only write is the ops_reports row. If a document_control row for this batch already exists, overwrite it so the result is idempotent.

success_criteria.summary: The agent produces exactly one ops_reports 'document_control' row for this batch. It contains the live-derived invoice and estimate sequence metadata (min/max/count/missing/sequence_ok), distinct owner/patient counts per ledger, cross-ledger numeric collisions, and a location breakdown by name. Every aggregate (counts, distinct counts, cross-collision count, location counts) is computed two independent ways (raw-row Python and SQL) and must agree with the agent's written row. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical to the seed snapshot.

checks.expect: Exactly one 'document_control' row for this batch with all required fields matching the live-derived values
Invoice count, distinct owner/patient counts, and location counts agree between raw-row Python and SQL
Estimate count, distinct owner/patient counts, and location counts agree between raw-row Python and SQL

hazards: The 'id' field on billing rows is not the document number: invoice ids are 1..260 and estimate ids are 1..100, while the document numbers are INV-1001..INV-1260 and EST-3001..EST-3100. A solution that uses the row id instead of parsing invoice_number/estimate_number will report the wrong min/max/count and a bogus missing list.

The ledgers contain rows of every status (invoices: paid, sent, draft; estimates: sent, draft, accepted, declined). The count must include all rows, not only 'active' ones. Excluding draft or other statuses changes the count and makes the sequence_ok field wrong.

The invoice numeric suffix range (1001..1260) and estimate numeric suffix range (3001..3100) do not overlap, so cross_collisions should be an empty list. A solution that compares numbers without the prefix or that hardcodes an empty list without checking will fail the cross-check if reseeded data ever has a real collision.

location_id is a foreign key to locations. The location_breakdown must use the live locations.name, not the raw location_id. The snapshot has 3 locations: Main Street Animal Hospital, Riverside Veterinary Clinic, and Cedar Park Animal Care Center.

Distinct owner and patient counts must be derived from live rows, not hardcoded. Invoices have 220 distinct owners and 260 distinct patients; estimates have 100 distinct owners and 100 distinct patients.
